en: The Sūtra of the Maṇḍala of the Eight Great Bodhisattvas.
By [the one holding the rank of] Kaifu Yitongsī, Tèjìn, Shì Hónglùqīng, Sùguōgōng,
with a fief of three thousand households, posthumously titled Sīkōng and conferred the honorary title Dàjiànzhèng (Great Mirror of Rectitude).
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Amoghavajra of Great Xingshan Temple, Possessor of Vast Wisdom, by Imperial Decree. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Bhagavat was dwelling in the palace of the Holy Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva on Mount Potalaka.
He was surrounded by hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas, preceding and following him.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva among the assembly named Ratnagarbha-candraprabha.
Rising from his seat, he adjusted his robes,
bared his right shoulder, bowed with palms joined,
and addressed the Bhagavān: "I have a slight doubt."
"I only pray that the Tathāgata will grant me permission to inquire.
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Ratnagarbha-candraprabha said:
"If a son or daughter of good family..."
How are the eight maṇḍalas established?
Furthermore, by relying on what dharma does one generate immeasurable merit,
enabling the practitioner to swiftly realize bodhi?
At that time, the Tathāgata praised the Bodhisattva Ratnagarbha-candraprabha, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
You are able to inquire about such a profound meaning."
It is for the sake of bringing benefit and peace to immeasurable and boundless sentient beings;
for the sake of purifying the three evil realms;
and for the sake of realizing incomparable, unsurpassed wisdom.
Listen well now:
if any sentient beings merely hear these secret words,
they shall attain long life and happiness.
"Noble son, there are eight maṇḍalas;
these are the profound essential teachings of the eight great bodhisattvas.
If there are sentient beings..."
If one recites these eight maṇḍalas once, established according to the Dharma,
all ten non-virtuous actions and the five heinous crimes, as well as the slandering of the Vaipulya sūtras, will be entirely extinguished.
All sought-after benefits and supreme aspirations shall be fully accomplished.
Then he spoke the Tathāgata’s secret mantra:
Oṃ mahāvīra svāhā. Within the maṇḍala, one should visualize the Tathāgata’s body as the color of pure gold.
Seated upon a lotus pedestal, endowed with the thirty-two marks, he next spoke the secret mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva:
*HŪṂ HĪḤ HAḤ PADMANAŚRĪYE SVĀHĀ*. One should then visualize [him] within the maṇḍala.
The noble Avalokiteśvara has a red body;
his left hand holds a lotus flower and his right hand performs the gesture of granting boons.
Within his crown is the Tathāgata Amitāyus.
Next, the secret mantra of Maitreya Bodhisattva is taught:
*Hā hīlī svāhā*. After the mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, one should visualize Maitreya Bodhisattva.
His golden body holds a *kamaṇḍalu* in his left hand and performs the gesture of fearlessness with his right;
upon his crown is a *stūpa*, and he sits in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*).
Next, the secret mantra (*mantra*) of the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha is taught as follows:
Āḥ-va-ya svāhā. Behind the Buddha, visualize the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja;
with his left hand, he holds a jewel at his heart.
From his right hand, he bestows an outflow of immeasurable jewels.
Next, the secret mantra of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva is spoken:
*Hrīḥ jaya svāhā*. To the left of Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva...
Visualize the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra,
wearing a crown of the five Buddhas, with a golden body;
his right hand holds a sword and his left hand performs the gesture of granting boons (*varada-mudrā*).
He sits in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*).
Next, the secret mantra of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi is proclaimed:
Oṃ vaṃ rava sa va ha. To the left of the Tathāgata, [he is situated].
Visualize the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
holding a vajra in his right hand and resting his left hand upon his hip,
wearing a crown of the five Buddhas.
His body is blue in color and he sits in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*).
Next, the secret mantra of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva is proclaimed:
*Śrī-jvala-gasa va ha*. [This is recited] before Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva.
Visualize the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta in the form of a five-crested youth,
holding a blue lotus flower in his left hand.
Within a lotus flower is a five-pronged vajra;
his right hand performs the gesture of granting boons (*varada-mudrā*);
his body is golden in color, and he sits in the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*).
Next, the secret mantra of the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin is spoken:
*Nivaraṇa svāhā*. [This is] to the right of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.
Visualize the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin,
with a golden body,
holding a wish-fulfilling banner in his left hand.
He sits in the half-lotus posture with his right hand in the gesture of granting boons (*varadamudrā*).
Next, the secret mantra of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva is proclaimed:
*Kṣāraharāja svāhā*. [This is recited] before the Tathāgata.
Visualize the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha,
his crown and necklaces radiant, his countenance serene and tranquil,
compassionately mindful of all sentient beings.
The left hand rests below the navel holding the *pātra*;
the right hand has its palm turned downward,
with the thumb and index finger joined to form the gesture of comforting all sentient beings.
This is the method for the visualization practice of making offerings to the maṇḍala of these eight great bodhisattvas.
If any son or daughter of good family upholds this sūtra of the eight maṇḍalas, [they shall attain...]
All karmic obstructions will be completely extinguished,
and they shall swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the assembly of great bodhisattvas and śrāvakas—
All the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings, having heard what the Buddha taught, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Eight Great Bodhisattvas’ Praise:
At the gate of the city of the palace of parinirvāṇa, You are able to shatter its door panels.
I prostrate to the Dharma-body of all Buddhas, the Savior of the World;
I prostrate to the Lotus-Handed One, from whose own hands flow pure waters that can remove the thirst of hungry ghosts,
the wish-fulfilling tree of the three realms.
With great compassion as his heart, he can extinguish the fire of anger;
I prostrate to the Honored One Maitreya. He can sever the bowstring of desire;
I prostrate to the Honored One Ākāśagarbha, whose wondrous wisdom is as tranquil as space.
Liberated from the stream of birth and death, I prostrate to the Son of the Buddha’s Heart.
You who can pacify the unwholesome minds of infinite sentient beings—
Samantabhadra, foremost son of the Sugata, I prostrate to you.
The dust of afflictions exhausted, he is like a servant;
Surpassing the summit of Māra’s army, I prostrate to Vajrapāṇi, Who can expound all vidyās;
I prostrate to Mañjuśrī, Who bears the form of a wondrous youth.
The lamp of wisdom shines forth universally,
dispelling the darkness of the three realms; Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin,
I therefore prostrate to the Honored One of inexhaustible wisdom, who can give rise to unfailing eloquence.
Just as the earth is the single, uninterrupted support for all sentient beings, so too is he—of firm wisdom and a treasury of compassion.
I prostrate my head to this Son of the Sugata, Kṣitigarbha; may the merit obtained from this praise be dedicated to all.
By means of these sentient beings, they become like those vessels praised [in the *Maṇḍala-sūtra* of the Eight Great Bodhisattvas].

Regarding the positions of the eight [deities] herein, as the text was erroneous, it has now been corrected according to the directions clarified in the *Recitation Method of the Uṣṇīṣavijayā* found in the Heng-fan edition.
